result.answer: Yes, as far as the evidence shows. The transfer message to WARD-B (bay BAY2-04, event time 09:20 UTC) read cleanly as a version 2.5.1 transfer message, and the route expects 2.5.1, so the versions match. It has everything the bed-management system needs for a transfer: patient MRN-T1 (HOSP), encounter ENC-T1, the event, the ward, the event time and the sending system. Its fields agree with the operation that was sent. The delivery did not fail because of the message. It failed because the bed-management system was unavailable (HTTP 503), and the system never said it rejected the content. Two caveats. The check covered the message's structure only. No separate site-rule review is on record, so Shutter cannot rule out a site-specific rule problem. Also, an acceptable message is still not worth resending: the system has since applied a later transfer to WARD-C (09:45 UTC). It keeps only the current placement, so resending would move the patient back. Whether the site wants a full history instead is a setting question (W1), not a message problem.
